items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I met Earl Bostic in ‘57, and he told me... I was playing a Brilhart mouthpiece, and he told me, “Get rid of that and get a Meyer.”

ctx.x: Can you speak about evolving towards that way of thinking about making records and your sound, and how it reflected the audiences you were playing for and what was going on around in the music, which was changing in the ‘60s...

I met Earl Bostic in ‘57, and he told me... I was playing a Brilhart mouthpiece, and he told me, “Get rid of that and get a Meyer.” He said a Meyer is better for the Selmer saxophone. He was right, and I got a different sound. Much clearer. I got the new sound, so I started playing slightly different. Not much. Slightly different.
